turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_toughness_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels,
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2 temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3 temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3
    cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1 temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 2 time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3
    time, Secondary treatment step 4 temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure
    temperature, Thermal exposure time) and the two measured objectives `yield
    strength (MPa)` and `toughness (J)` (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_toughness_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose
    objectives were NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same
    process/composition columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH toughness (J). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), toughness (J)) plane, so a set of mutually
non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates that are
all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll systematically analyze the training data to identify patterns that predict high yield strength and high toughness, then match pool candidates to those patterns.

## Step 1: Identify the Pareto frontier in training data

Let me extract the non-dominated points (high YS AND high toughness):

Key high-performing training points:
- **600 MPa, 350 J**: Fe~66.9, Cr~12.5, Ni~8, Mn~8.5, C~0.37, V~1.4, Nb~0.35, Mo~1.25 → austenitic Mn steel, HT 1150°C, AH 660/790°C
- **380 MPa, 370 J**: Fe~51.8, Cr~24.5, Ni~16.5, Mn~6, C~0.12 → high-Cr/Ni austenitic
- **350 MPa, 323 J**: Fe~86.1, Cr~13, C~0.04 → ferritic/martensitic
- **270 MPa, 350 J**: Fe~41.7, Cr~23.5, Ni~27.5, Mo~2.75, Cu~3 → high-Ni austenitic
- **280 MPa, 300 J**: Fe~54.7, Cr~23.5, Ni~18.5, C~0.2 → austenitic
- **270 MPa, 294 J**: Fe~68, Cr~18, Ni~12, C~0.06 → 304-type
- **710 MPa, 230 J**: Fe~94.8, Cr~2.35, Mo~1, C~0.255, V~0.4 → low-alloy high-strength
- **725 MPa, 215 J**: Fe~67.1, Ni~18, Mo~5 → maraging-type
- **446 MPa, 189 J**: Fe~97.7, Cr~0.55, Mo~0.5, C~0.125
- **570 MPa, 160 J**: Fe~85.5, Cr~10.75, Ni~0.75, Mo~0.95, V~0.3

The Pareto front spans roughly:
- Low YS / very high toughness: ~270 MPa / 350 J
- Mid YS / high toughness: ~380 MPa / 370 J, ~600 MPa / 350 J
- High YS / moderate toughness: ~710 MPa / 230 J, ~725 MPa / 215 J

## Step 2: Match pool candidates to training analogs

**c010** (Fe~41.3, Cr~23.5, Ni~27, Mo~2.75, Cu~3, C~0.06): Very similar to training point (270 MPa, 350 J) — high-Ni/Cr austenitic, no aging → expect ~270 MPa, ~350 J. **Excellent toughness end.**

**c017** (Fe~60.7, Cr~14, Ni~19, Nb~1.1, W~2.4, B~0.025, HT 1170°C, AH 750°C): Similar to training (210-270 MPa, 110-130 J range) but with higher HT temp. Closest analog: 220 MPa/100 J. Moderate.

**c053** (Fe~60.7, Cr~14, Ni~19, Nb~1.1, W~2.4, HT 1170°C, AH 725°C): Similar to training (220 MPa, 100 J). Moderate.

**c085** (Fe~94.8, Cr~2.35, Mo~1, C~0.255, V~0.4, HT 1040°C, then 960°C, then 675°C temper): Training analog with 3-stage HT gave 710 MPa/230 J. **High YS, good toughness.**

**c094** (Fe~85.9, Cr~10.75, Ni~0.6, Mo~0.7, V~0.325, C~0.155, HT 1075°C, temper 675°C short): Training analogs at 675-700°C temper gave 700-750 MPa / 60-70 J. Moderate toughness.

**c050** (Fe~68.2, Cr~12, Ni~8, Mo~1.25, Mn~8, C~0.37, V~1.3, Nb~0.35, HT 1150°C, AH 725°C, aging 550°C): Training analog (Mn-steel) at 550°C aging gave 500 MPa/34 J. Less ideal.

**c069** (Fe~68.2, Cr~12, Ni~8, Mo~1.25, Mn~8, C~0.37, V~1.3, Nb~0.35, HT 1150°C, AH 725°C, aging 650°C/5000h): Training analog at 650°C/5000h gave 650 MPa/40 J. Better YS.

**c066** (Fe~41.6, Cr~15, Ni~35, Ti~2.8, Al~1.05, W~3.2, HT 1160°C, aging 750°C/10000h): Training analog gave 670 MPa/31 J. High YS but low toughness.

**c026** (Fe~53.9, Cr~15, Ni~23.5, Ti~1.6, W~4.5, HT 1140°C, AH 740°C): Novel composition. Similar to Fe~40-42/Ni~35-36 class but with less Ni. Expect moderate YS ~500-600 MPa, moderate toughness.

**c044** (Fe~60.5, Cr~11.25, Ni~23, Mo~1.3, Ti~2.9, Al~0.4, HT 1120°C, AH 735°C): Training analog (1000 MPa, 100 J). **Very high YS, moderate toughness.**

**c060** (Fe~60.5, Cr~11.25, Ni~23, Mo~1.3, Ti~2.9, Al~0.4, HT 1120°C, AH 845°C/710°C): Training analog gave 1000 MPa/100 J. **High YS end.**

**c008** (Fe~64.9, Cr~11.25, Ni~19.5, Ti~2.9, Al~0.4, HT 1175°C, AH 750°C): Training analog at 1100°C/AH 750°C gave 710 MPa/114 J. **Good balance.**

**c024** (Fe~42.3, Cr~15, Ni~36, Ti~1.3, W~3.15, HT 1180°C, AH 780°C/730°C): Training analogs with double AH gave ~350-430 MPa, 40-75 J. Moderate.

**c099** (Fe~54.7, Cr~23.5, Ni~18.5, C~0.2, HT 1180°C, AH 800°C): Training analog gave 280 MPa/300 J. **High toughness, moderate YS.**

**c002** (Fe~68.2, Cr~18, Ni~12, Ti~0.3, HT 1075°C, aging 700°C/10000h): Training analog at 700°C/10000h gave ~245 MPa/214 J. Moderate.

**c038** (Fe~66.1, Cr~18, Ni~12, Nb~0.95, C~0.08, HT 1020°C, aging 600°C/10000h): Training analog gave 230 MPa/185 J. Good toughness.

## Step 3: Build the best Pareto-spanning set of 5

I need candidates that span the frontier well. Key regions:
1. **Very high toughness / moderate YS** (~270-380 MPa, 300-370 J)
2. **High YS / moderate toughness** (~700-1000 MPa, 100-230 J)
3. **Mid-range balance** (~500-600 MPa, 150-200 J)

Best candidates:

1. **c010** — High-Ni/Cr austenitic, no aging → ~270 MPa, ~350 J (toughness anchor)
